# Nonatomic common curvature measures replace smooth arc bumps

This extends the signed perturbation and Hessian-convexification mechanism
of nonsmooth-direct-budget-arc-stress.md. The support compatibility and cap
membership must still be stable on the normal interval. No global finite
decomposition of contact sets is asserted.

## 1. Hypotheses

Let h_z be planar convex support functions on a stable open normal interval
I, and let

    R_z=h_z+h_z''

denote their nonnegative curvature MEASURES, with distributional derivatives.
The finite active support relations have common coefficient kernel L and
hold identically on I. Other support constraints have positive gaps on the
compact intervals used below. Every specified cap has constant strict
membership on each affected boundary arc, including the whole exposed edge
when a normal exposes an edge.

Assume a nonzero finite NONATOMIC measure nu on I is dominated by every
R_z, after a fixed positive rescaling if necessary. More generally, if only
the indices in J share such a measure, use

    L_J=L intersect {v:v_z=0 outside J}

in every assertion. A common measure for no admissible nonzero coordinate
direction gives no perturbation. Domination is an explicit assumption; it
is not inferred from the separate positivity of curvature measures.

## 2. Compactly supported Green potentials

Choose an interval [a,b] compactly contained in I, with b-a<pi and positive
nu mass. For a bounded signed density psi supported there set

    phi(theta)=integral_(a<=s<=theta) sin(theta-s) psi(s) dnu(s).

Impose the two linear constraints

    integral cos(s) psi(s)dnu(s)=0,
    integral sin(s) psi(s)dnu(s)=0.                           (1)

Then phi vanishes before a and after b. Its derivative is the corresponding
cosine integral, and (1) also makes that derivative vanish after b. Since nu
has no atoms, phi is C1; it belongs to H0^1([a,b]), and distributionally

    phi''+phi=psi nu.                                       (2)

Impose in addition the finitely many equations

    integral phi dR_z=0           for every fiber z.         (3)

There exists a nonzero bounded psi satisfying (1),(3). To see this without
an infinite-dimensional existence claim, choose |P|+3 disjoint measurable
sets of positive nu mass inside [a,b]. Put psi equal to an independent
constant on each. Conditions (1),(3) are at most |P|+2 homogeneous linear
equations in those constants; (3) is linear by Fubini with a bounded sine
kernel. A nonzero solution gives a nonzero signed measure psi nu and hence,
by (2), a nonzero phi.

The interval Poincare identity in candidate 2d6d202be366ee4e gives

    Q(phi)=integral(phi^2-phi'^2)<0.                          (4)

Rescaling psi and phi realizes any prescribed negative value of Q.

## 3. Signed convexity and compatibility are exact

For v in L, set h_z(t)=h_z+t v_z phi. Its curvature measure is

    R_z(t)=R_z+t v_z psi nu.

Since nu<=R_z and psi is bounded, this measure is nonnegative for BOTH
signs of t whenever |t|max_z|v_z| ||psi||_infinity<1. The support functions
therefore remain convex support functions. One may justify this familiar
planar criterion directly by the monotonically turning boundary curve, or
by smooth circular convolution of the nonnegative curvature measure and
passage to the uniform support-function limit.

The active support relations stay equalities because v is in their kernel.
The compact perturbation is uniformly small, so the other strict gaps
remain positive. Outside [a,b] both phi and phi' vanish. The moved boundary
points and any exposed-edge endpoints have displacement bounded by
|t v_z|(|phi|+|phi'|), so the strict cap membership on the affected arcs is
preserved for small |t|. No cap line is crossed by a changed region.

The same proof works with L_J and v_z=0 outside the common-measure indices.

## 4. Exact area Hessians and arbitrary disjoint conic sums

For every planar convex support function h, the area identity holds in H1:

    area(K)=1/2 integral(h^2-h'^2).

It follows from the smooth identity by circular convolution of h and H1
convergence; the corresponding convex bodies converge in Hausdorff distance.
Applying the quadratic identity to h_z+t v_z phi gives exactly

    area(K_z(t))'=v_z integral phi dR_z=0,
    area(K_z(t))''=v_z^2 Q(phi).                             (5)

Every specified cap area has the same derivative multiplied by its constant
membership indicator on this arc. Thus all first cap masses vanish as well.

A nonzero nonatomic measure has arbitrarily many pairwise disjoint compact
subintervals of positive measure: choose any prescribed finite number of
distinct support points and then disjoint small neighborhoods, with endpoints
chosen to carry no mass. On each interval perform Sections2 and3 separately.
The resulting potentials and their derivatives have disjoint supports, so
their mixed area Hessian terms are zero. Hence all finite conic sums of the
same vectors

    (B0(v),Bj(v))=(-sum_z v_z^2,-sum_z I_jz v_z^2), v in L

are realized by one actual compatible signed perturbation, exactly as in
the smooth construction.

The direct-budget proof now applies verbatim, using finite-dimensional
bases of the first-mass feature images of these admissible potentials.
It supplies ONE collection lambda_j>=0 with sum lambda_j=1/beta and

    sum_z [1-sum_j lambda_j I_jz] v_z^2>=0 for every v in L.  (6)

With partial common-measure support replace L by L_J. This proves the PSD
conclusion without a smooth positive curvature density.

## 5. What first-order annihilation does and does not yet say

For the same stress, first-order annihilation is initially

    sum_z W_z integral delta h_z dR_z=0

for the ADMISSIBLE Green-potential accelerations just constructed. On a
singular overlap measure these are not all arbitrary smooth compact support
variations. Therefore the earlier pointwise statement that the entire
curvature vector lies in a fixed nullspace must not be copied without a
separate density or potential argument.

One sufficient additional condition is that nu has full support on I. Here
is an explicit justification. Fix v in L and put mu=sum_z W_z v_z R_z. On a
compact [a,b] every bounded psi satisfying (1) is an admissible acceleration
(orthogonality (3) is unnecessary for first-order tests). By Fubini,

    integral phi dmu = integral psi(s) U(s)dnu(s),
    U(s)=integral_(s<=theta<=b) sin(theta-s)dmu(theta).

The first expression vanishes for every such psi. Thus U is a linear
combination of sin(s),cos(s) nu-almost everywhere: this is the elementary
annihilator statement for the kernel of the two moment maps, proved by
factoring the linear functional through their finite-dimensional image.
The function U is continuous. Full support makes equality hold everywhere
in (a,b), and distributionally U''+U=mu there. Consequently mu vanishes on
(a,b). Exhausting I proves the measure identity

    sum_z W_z v_z R_z=0 on I for every v in L.                (7)

Taking Radon--Nikodym densities relative to sum_z R_z, the active linear
relations and (7) put their curvature-density vector in the nullspace of
the PSD form (6) almost everywhere. Without such a justified enrichment of
the test class, only (6) and annihilation on the admissible potentials are
claimed.
